Action Plan:
1. Prescribe stronger analgesia for current headache episode:
   • Advise correct ibuprofen dosing (up to 400 mg × 2 tablets, three times daily; dose/route/frequency not fully documented).  
   • Offer prescription for Naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented) ± adjunctive Paracetamol or Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
2. Instruct patient to keep a detailed headache diary (timing, severity, triggers, analgesic use) until review.
3. Schedule follow-up appointment in 1–2 weeks; advise earlier review for any red-flag symptoms (visual loss, focal weakness, speech difficulty, persistent vomiting, sudden escalation of pain).
4. Recommend repeat eye examination to address possible eye-strain contribution.
5. Discuss possible need for prophylactic migraine therapy at follow-up if headaches become recurrent.
6. Safety-net: seek urgent care if headache worsens, new neurological deficits develop, or vision changes occur.
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: 3-day history of worsening headache.  
• HPI:
  – Onset: gradual, began ~3 days ago at work.  
  – Location: diffuse, maximal around right eye.  
  – Character: baseline dull pain with intermittent sharp exacerbations.  
  – Severity: 8/10.  
  – Course: constant with fluctuations, getting worse each day.  
  – Associated symptoms: photophobia (light hurts), “shooting lights” at onset, nausea without vomiting, difficulty concentrating.  
  – Alleviating/Aggravating: Sleep and ibuprofen (3 tablets/day) provide little relief; screen brightness reduction helps tolerance.  
  – No fever, neck stiffness, rash, focal weakness, speech disturbance, trauma.
• Past medical history: none reported; no prior personal migraines.  
• Family history: Mother and sister suffer recurrent migraines.  
• Medications: None regular; self-administered ibuprofen (dose/frequency not fully documented).  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies.  
• Social history: 26-year-old female; IT professional with prolonged computer use; lives with three housemates; social smoker; social alcohol intake; mild work stress.  
• No contraceptive pill use documented.

Objective:
• No physical examination or vital signs recorded (tele-consultation).  
• No investigations performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute severe headache (likely migraine):
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Migraine with possible visual aura (DDx item: “Migraine (possibly with aura)” – High likelihood).
   - Differential diagnosis:  
     • Tension-type headache – Medium likelihood (support: diffuse dull pain, work stress; oppose: photophobia, visual aura).  
     • Acute sinusitis – Low–Medium likelihood (support: periorbital pain; oppose: no nasal symptoms).  
     • Idiopathic intracranial hypertension – Low likelihood (support: age/sex; oppose: no obesity, papilledema).  
     • Subarachnoid hemorrhage – Very Low likelihood (support: severe pain; oppose: gradual onset, no neuro deficits).
   - Investigations planned: None immediately; monitor with headache diary; consider further work-up if atypical features emerge.
   - Treatment planned: Optimise NSAID dosing; prescribe Naproxen ± Paracetamol or Codeine; advise rest, hydration, darkened environment.
   - Relevant referrals: Neurology consideration only if headaches become frequent or exhibit red-flag features.

2. Possible eye strain / need for vision assessment:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Refractive strain contributing to headache.
   - Differential diagnosis: Under-corrected vision, screen fatigue.
   - Investigations planned: Routine optometry eye test.
   - Treatment planned: Adjust spectacle prescription if indicated; maintain appropriate screen ergonomics.
   - Relevant referrals: Optometrist for comprehensive eye examination.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected elements: Objective exam findings (vitals, neurological exam), full medication doses/routes/frequencies, menstrual/contraceptive history, vaccination status.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor conversational fillers, no significant inaudible sections.
